summary: NIFTY 50 on NSE_INDEX (token 26000 on Tradejini's NSE segment), one client at Quote and one at LTP: no volume, trade time or book; the change Tradejini sends.

deviations.reason: The web's Tradejini adapter puts its subscription mode number (1, 2, 3) in data.mode; the desktop sends the label (ltp, quote, full). Phase B: follows the web adapter through wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Tradejini: the number).

Tradejini sends the trade time in epoch seconds; the web formats it with the server's local time zone into a text such as "2025-11-05 14:25:31" (nxtradstream.py datefmt) and sends that as ltt, where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends epoch ms, and leaves ltt out when Tradejini sent no trade time, where the web sends null (Quote, Depth) or "" (LTP).
An index has no trades: its L1 carries no ltq, and the web sends last_quantity 0 (message.get("ltq", 0)), an invented zero; the desktop's index frame leaves it out (rules.md: no invented data).
As last_quantity: an index L1 carries no atp, and the web sends average_price 0.
An index's L1 carries no OI; the web sends oi 0. The desktop's index frame carries no OI.

The web's Tradejini adapter sends an index's change only under its own names (change, change_percent, percent_change); the desktop adds price_change, the canonical name of the recorded Zerodha transcript. Phase B: follows the web adapter through wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Tradejini: no price_change).
